overview.summary: Mobile app developers design, build and maintain apps for phones and tablets.
overview.problems: They turn ideas such as ordering food, learning a language or banking safely into apps that work smoothly on small screens.
overview.worksWith: Designers, product managers, other developers, testers and sometimes customers.
overview.workplaces: Technology companies, start-ups, agencies, banks and other businesses, and freelance or remote work.

timeline.title: Team stand-up
timeline.description: The team shares progress and blockers and agrees the day's tasks.
timeline.why: Short check-ins keep everyone lined up.

timeline.title: Building features
timeline.description: The developer writes code for new screens and actions and runs the app on a phone or emulator.
timeline.why: Features must work smoothly on small screens and many devices.

timeline.title: Testing on different devices
timeline.description: The developer checks how the app behaves on different phone sizes, software versions and slow connections.
timeline.why: A feature that works on one phone can fail on another.

timeline.title: Fixing bugs
timeline.description: The developer reads crash reports and user reviews, finds the cause and fixes it.

timeline.title: Design and code review
timeline.description: The developer checks designs with the designer and reviews teammates' code.
timeline.why: Reviews catch mistakes and keep the app consistent.

timeline.title: Updates and app store rules
timeline.description: New phone software or store rules mean the app needs changes, and releases are prepared carefully.
timeline.why: An app that is not kept up to date can stop working or be removed.

responsibilities: Testing on different devices and versions
Keeping apps fast, secure and respectful of privacy
Working with designers and other developers
challenges: There are many different devices and software versions to support.
Phone and store rules change often.
Apps must be fast and use little battery.
Some bugs are hard to reproduce.
Tools change constantly, so learning never stops.
workEnvironment: Mostly desk and computer based, in offices or remotely, often in small teams. Hours are often regular, with busier periods before releases. Some developers work as freelancers or build their own apps.
rewards: Seeing people use something you built on their own phone
Options to work for a company, freelance or build your own app
Skills that can be shown through projects
tradeoffs: Constant change in tools and rules
Job requirements and pay that vary by country and employer

activity.title: Design and build a tiny app
steps: Pick a simple idea, such as a quiz or a checklist.
Sketch three screens on paper and show them to a friend.
If you can, build a basic version with a free beginner app builder such as MIT App Inventor.
Ask two people to try it and note where they got stuck.
Fix one thing and note whether building and testing felt enjoyable.
activity.outcome: You practise the plan, build, test and improve cycle used in app development.
activity.safety: Do not collect other people's personal data, do not publish the app publicly without an adult, and use only your own images and text.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
